title: Safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated thimerosal-free influenza vaccine in infants and children.
ehr_evidence: An AE diary card was used to record solicited local and systemic AEs during the 6 days following the day of vaccination.
summary: Prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial evaluating the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a thimerosal-free inactivated influenza vaccine in healthy children aged 6 months to <9 years.
key_findings: A maximum intensity of severe was reported for injection site pain and fever by only 3.0% and 3.4% of participants, respectively.
≥95% of both younger and older children achieved seroprotection after dose 2.
Of those seronegative at baseline, 97% became seroprotected after dose 1 against A/H3N2 versus 15% for A/H1N1 and 22% for B.
Only one participant had a confirmed case of influenza B after the booster vaccination, but the specimen was compromised during transportation.
captured_features: solicited local and systemic adverse events
study_design: prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial
population: healthy children aged 6 months to <9 years
limitations: lack of a placebo control group
compromised laboratory specimen for one confirmed influenza case
